title: Grind Test
purpose: Provocation test for thumb carpometacarpal (CMC 1, trapeziometacarpal) osteoarthritis.
procedure: Patient sitting, hand on the table, stabilised with one hand; wrist and metacarpals neutral. Grasp the thumb metacarpal and rotate it while applying axial pressure onto the trapezium.
positive: Any pain, even slight, or crepitus at the base of the thumb.

accuracy.source: Sela et al. (text 2017, reference 2019, J Hand Ther), vs Eaton-Littler radiographic staging

notes: Source: moderate clinical value; confirms CMC OA but a negative test does not exclude radiographic OA, and OA remains a clinical diagnosis. Radiographic prevalence of thumb OA reaches 90% by age 80. ⚠ Text cites Sela 2017, reference list 2019 (same for the pressure-shear, MC flexion and MC extension pages).

title: Pressure Shear Test
purpose: Provocation test for thumb CMC osteoarthritis.
structure: Thumb CMC joint; anterior oblique ligament.
procedure: Patient sitting, hand stabilised on the table, wrist and metacarpals neutral. Apply pressure over the anterior oblique ligament and create a shearing force across the CMC joint by rocking the metacarpal across the trapezium.
positive: Any pain, even slight, in the basal joint region of the thumb.

accuracy.source: Sela et al. (text 2017, reference 2019, J Hand Ther)

notes: Source: moderate clinical value despite excellent figures, because the test was performed last of four provocative tests (possible sensitisation) and this was the first formal study, in a surgical setting. Source typo 'repots'.

title: MC Flexion Test
purpose: Provocation test for thumb CMC osteoarthritis.
procedure: Patient sitting, hand stabilised on the table, wrist and metacarpals neutral. Move the thumb metacarpal into flexion.
positive: Pain, even slight, in the basal region of the thumb.

accuracy.source: Sela et al. (text 2017, reference 2019, J Hand Ther), vs Eaton-Littler staging

notes: Source: moderate clinical value; good to confirm, negative does not exclude. The page lists the four Eaton-Littler radiographic stages.

title: MC Extension Test
purpose: Provocation test for thumb CMC osteoarthritis.
procedure: Patient sitting, hand stabilised on the table, wrist and metacarpals neutral. Move the thumb metacarpal into extension.
positive: Pain, even slight, in the basal region of the thumb.

accuracy.source: Sela et al. (text 2017, reference 2019, J Hand Ther)

notes: Source: moderate clinical value; good to confirm, negative does not exclude.

title: Traction-Shift Test
purpose: Subluxation-relocation test for thumb CMC osteoarthritis.
procedure: Single-handed technique: apply longitudinal traction to the thumb, then alternate dorsal and palmar pressure over the base of the metacarpal to provoke subluxation and relocation of the joint.

accuracy.source: Choa et al. 2014 (J Hand Surg Eur), case-control vs grind test

notes: Source: moderate clinical value; confirms CMC OA, negative does not exclude radiographic OA.

title: Adduction Test
purpose: Provocation test for thumb CMC osteoarthritis.
procedure: Patient sitting opposite you, hand on the table, elbow flexed 90 degrees, forearm neutral. Support the ulnar side of the hand to keep the wrist neutral and prevent ulnar deviation; rest your thumb dorsally over the head of the thumb metacarpal and firmly direct an adduction force downward until the thumb metacarpal lies parallel to the index metacarpal or a firm end-feel is reached.
positive: Reproduction of the patient's pain at the TMC joint.

accuracy.source: Gelberman et al. 2015 (J Hand Surg Am); inter-rater kappa 0.79

notes: Source: moderate clinical value until validated in other settings (novel test, study limitations). The page repeats its limitation sentence twice.

title: Extension Stress Test
purpose: Provocation test for thumb CMC osteoarthritis.
procedure: Patient sitting opposite you, hand on the table, elbow flexed 90 degrees, forearm neutral. Support the ulnar side of the hand to keep the wrist neutral; place your thumb along the radial aspect of the distal thumb metacarpal, 5-10 mm proximal to the thumb MCP joint, and firmly extend the thumb until the metacarpal lies parallel to the palm or a firm end-feel is reached.
positive: Reproduction of the patient's pain at the TMC joint.

accuracy.source: Gelberman et al. 2015 (J Hand Surg Am); inter-rater kappa 0.84

notes: Source: moderate clinical value until validated in other settings.

title: Finkelstein Test
purpose: Hallmark test for de Quervain tenosynovitis (first dorsal compartment: extensor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis longus), in the staged version of Dawson & Mudgal 2010.
structure: Tendon sheath of EPB and APL at the radial styloid (first dorsal compartment).
procedure: Forearm neutral, ulnar side of the forearm on the table, ulnar side of the hand hanging off the edge. Stage 1 (acute): gravity-assisted gentle active ulnar deviation. Stage 2: gently apply a passive ulnar deviation force to the hand (stretch across the first dorsal compartment). Stage 3 (original Finkelstein, chronic cases): grasp the thumb and passively flex it into the palm.
positive: Pain aggravation at the tip of the radial styloid at any stage.

accuracy.source: none; page states no validity values are known

notes: Source: questionable clinical value. The staged approach is hypothesised to produce fewer false positives than Eichhoff's test, which is often confused with Finkelstein's test in the literature (Elliott 1992). Also called gamer's thumb / blackberry thumb.

title: Eichhoff’s Test
purpose: Provocation test for de Quervain tenosynovitis; the version commonly mislabelled as Finkelstein's test.
structure: EPB and APL tendons forming the radial border of the anatomical snuffbox.
procedure: Patient's extended arm rests on the table with the wrist hanging off the edge. Patient makes a fist with the thumb inside; stabilise the forearm and gently deviate the wrist to the ulnar side.
positive: Pain over the EPB and APL tendons.

accuracy.source: Goubau et al. 2014 (J Hand Surg Eur), vs ultrasound; only study

notes: Source: questionable clinical value; very provocative with many false positives, so the staged Finkelstein test is recommended instead (Elliott 1992; Wu et al. 2018). ⚠ The page text repeats two paragraphs of the Finkelstein page ('If the second step is still not provocating...') that describe the Finkelstein stages, not Eichhoff's test. The page spells the author 'Goubeau' in the text and says the tendons form the 'medial base' of the snuffbox.

title: WHAT Test
purpose: Wrist Hyperflexion and Abduction of the Thumb test for de Quervain tenosynovitis: isolates APL and EPB with the patient in control of the pain.
structure: APL and EPB tendons and the pulley of the first extensor compartment.
procedure: Patient maximally flexes the wrist within pain limits while keeping the thumb fully extended and abducted (extension = towards the radial side in the plane of the palm; abduction = away from the palm). Apply a gradually increasing abduction resistance to the thumb; when the patient can no longer hold, they release and the test ends.
positive: Pain on resisted pressure against the examiner.

accuracy.source: Goubau et al. 2014 (J Hand Surg Eur), vs ultrasound; only study

notes: Source: moderate clinical value to rule out de Quervain's, not useful to confirm. Passive tests (Eichhoff, Finkelstein) also stress unrelated joints (radioscaphoid, scaphotrapezial, trapeziometacarpal, MCP) and ligaments, giving false positives.

title: Allen Test
purpose: Assess patency of the radial and ulnar arteries (hand circulation).
structure: Radial and ulnar arteries, palmar arches.
procedure: Patient opens and closes the hand quickly several times, then squeezes it tightly while you compress the radial and ulnar arteries with your thumbs. Patient opens the hand; release the radial artery and watch the colour return. Repeat releasing the ulnar artery. Always compare both hands.
positive: Blood does not stream back quickly (no prompt return of red colour) after releasing the artery.

accuracy.source: Jarvis et al. 2000 (Ann Thorac Surg), radial artery selection for coronary bypass

notes: Jarvis concluded that no cut-off performs satisfactorily and Doppler ultrasound should be used instead. Source writes the figures with comma decimals ('54,5%', '91,7%', '79,6%', '75,8%'). Companion: digital blood flow test.

title: Digital Blood Flow Test
purpose: Capillary refill check for arterial insufficiency of the fingers.
procedure: Compress the patient's nail bed and note the time for the colour to return.
positive: Colour does not return within 3 seconds.

accuracy.source: none; reference is Magee 2014 textbook (Orthopedic Physical Assessment)

notes: Companion: Allen test for the radial and ulnar arteries.

title: Upper Limb Tension Test 1
purpose: Neurodynamic test (ULNT A) biased to the median nerve, anterior interosseous nerve and C5-C7 roots; used for cervical radiculopathy and carpal tunnel syndrome. The upper-limb equivalent of the straight leg raise.
structure: Median nerve, anterior interosseous nerve, nerve roots C5-C7.
procedure: Test the good side first. Depress the shoulder, abduct the arm to 110 degrees, flex the elbow 90 degrees, externally rotate the shoulder to 90 degrees, extend the wrist and fingers, then slowly extend the elbow. Sensitise with contralateral cervical lateral flexion.
positive: Reproduction of the patient's familiar arm symptoms (shooting pain, paraesthesia); some authors also score a marked loss of mobility (>10 degrees) as positive.
notes: Filed by the source under Cervical Spine Assessment; collected here with ULTT 2-4 by owner decision (all four pages embed the same video rir6x6Iiqc4 at different timestamps). ULTT1 is also listed by the source as a CTS test. ⚠ The ULTT1 page does not state the positive criterion; the criterion above is taken from the ULTT2-4 pages.

title: Upper Limb Tension Test 2
purpose: Neurodynamic test (ULNT B) biased to the median, axillary and musculocutaneous nerves.
structure: Median nerve, axillary nerve, musculocutaneous nerve.
procedure: Same as ULTT1 except the arm is abducted only 10 degrees: depress the shoulder, flex the elbow 90 degrees, extend the wrist and fingers, slowly extend the elbow while watching the patient's face.
positive: Reproduction of familiar arm symptoms (shooting pain, paraesthesia). Some authors score the test negative in case of a marked decrease of mobility (>10 degrees).

accuracy.source: Apelby-Albrecht et al. 2013 (J Manipulative Physiol Ther), cervical radiculopathy; page text writes '(2009'

notes: ⚠ Text cites Apelby-Albrecht et al. (2009; the reference list gives 2013. Shares the video with ULTT 1, 3 and 4 (timestamp 94 s). Test the good side first.

title: Upper Limb Tension Test 3
purpose: Neurodynamic test (ULNT C) biased to the radial nerve.
procedure: Depress the shoulder, abduct the arm 10 degrees, flex the wrist and fingers, pronate the forearm, flex the elbow to 90 degrees, then slowly extend the elbow. Sensitise with contralateral lateral flexion.
positive: Reproduction of familiar arm symptoms (shooting pain, paraesthesia). Some authors score the test negative in case of a marked decrease of mobility (>10 degrees).

accuracy.sensitivity: 43% (Apelby-Albrecht 2013); 72% (Wainner 2003, as written on the page for 'ULTT1 or ULTTA')
accuracy.source: Apelby-Albrecht et al. 2013; Wainner et al. 2003 (Spine)

notes: ⚠ The page's Wainner sentence says 'the ULTT1 or ULTTA has a sensitivity of 72% and a specificity of 33%' on the ULTT3 page; the ULTT1 page gives 97%/22% for ULTT1 and the ULTT4 page gives 72%/33% for ULTT4, so the sentence appears to be a copy error. Shares the video with ULTT 1, 2 and 4 (timestamp 139 s).

title: Upper Limb Tension Test 4
purpose: Neurodynamic test (ULNT D) biased to the ulnar nerve and the C8-T1 roots (ulnar nerve entrapment).
structure: Ulnar nerve, nerve roots C8 and T1.
procedure: Depress the shoulder, abduct the arm to 90 degrees, extend the fingers and wrist, supinate the forearm, then bring the patient's hand to the ear. Sensitise with contralateral lateral flexion.
positive: Reproduction of familiar arm symptoms (shooting pain, paraesthesia). Some authors score the test negative in case of a marked decrease of mobility (>10 degrees).

accuracy.source: Wainner et al. 2003 (Spine); Apelby-Albrecht et al. 2013, cervical radiculopathy

notes: Filed by the source under 'Wrist & Hand' (not Assessment). Shares the video with ULTT 1-3 (timestamp 178 s). Test the good side first.
